summary: Runner metrics-exporter cert rotation misroutes runner heartbeats causing job stalls
description:
Issue summary: After a scheduled rotation of the metrics-exporter TLS certs (2026-03-09 03:00 UTC), a subset of self-hosted CI runners started to stop reporting heartbeats to the runner-manager and were subsequently evicted from job assignment pools. Impact: Several nightly release and canary builds observed elongated queue times (median queue increase ~4x) and 12% of in-flight ephemeral jobs showed 'runner unreachable' errors. No data exfiltration suspected; operational availability degraded for release windows.

Environment: Production (us-west cluster of self-hosted runners). Metrics exporter sits in front of runner heartbeats to feed autoscaling and health checks. Rotation was performed via automated rotation job (release-eng kubejob) that updated cert secret and restarted metrics-exporter pods.

Observed behavior: After rotation, metrics-exporter started responding with 503 on /heartbeat-proxy for ~30% of runners. The runner-manager incorrectly routed heartbeat traffic to the old cert-bound proxy endpoint due to an in-memory mapping TTL mismatch, causing TLS handshake failures and eventual runner eviction.

Expected behavior: Rotation should update both cert secrets and the in-memory proxy mapping atomically or with a short synchronization window so active runners keep streaming heartbeats uninterrupted.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Deploy rotation job that updates secret "metrics-exporter-cert". 2) Restart metrics-exporter deployment. 3) Observe runner-manager logs for TLS handshake errors and runner disconnects while jobs are active. (Repro rate observed ~30% under steady-state job load).
steps_to_reproduce: Trigger automated cert rotation for metrics-exporter secret in prod (simulate via canary namespace).
Restart metrics-exporter pods while 200+ runners are active in the pool.
Observe runner-manager and proxy logs for TLS handshake and routing mismatch errors.
logs: 2026-03-09T03:12:41Z runner-manager ERROR tls: remote error: tls: bad certificate (peer=runner-az1-004)
2026-03-09T03:12:43Z metrics-exporter WARN proxymap: stale-mapping-detected key=runner-az1-004 last_update=2026-03-09T02:59:10Z
curl -v https://metrics-proxy.internal/heartbeat-proxy --tlsv1.2 -> SSL: certificate subject mismatch (expected new cert)
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: cert rotation updated Kubernetes secret and restarted pods but did not flush in-memory proxy mapping used by runner-manager. Evidence: proxymap logs show stale entries with TTL 15m; rotation job updated secret but mapping clean job is a separate cron (30m). Reproduce locally by forcing rotation and checking mapping TTL expiration; confirmed that mappings referencing old endpoint remained for ~18 minutes, during which runner heartbeats failed when leader routing switched to new pods. Secondary hypothesis: load-balancer sticky routing kept some heartbeats pinned to an old pod with rotated cert; however cloud LB logs show round-robin after restart, reducing likelihood.

Related artifacts: linked INT-70123 (ci-runner-permission-lockout-during-credential-rollforward) -- similar timing pattern during bulk rotates; relevant PRs: github.com/redwood/release-tools/pull/412 (rotation job change), github.com/redwood/runner-manager/pull/988 (proxy mapping TTL change proposed). Confluence runbook: "Release cert rotation checklist" updated to note proxymap flush step.
workaround:
1) Manually trigger proxymap flush job post-rotation: kubectl -n release-eng apply -f proxymap-flush-job.yaml. 2) Temporarily increase proxymap TTL to 1m (reduces window) via deployment env var PROXYMAP_TTL_SECONDS. 3) For immediate recovery, curl each affected metrics-exporter pod to force TLS negotiation and then scale runners by +10% to absorb evicted jobs.

Customer-facing impact: Internal only (no external customers affected), but release pipelines delayed ~30-90 minutes for some teams.
current_actions: SRE: backport runner-manager proxymap flush on rotation (RFC in PR 988).
Release Eng: update rotation job to call proxymap flush as a final step; roll out to staging for 24h canary.
DevExp: notify release squads and queue owners about temporary TTL change and expected recovery windows.
